notes: kb/Work PB5173 landed. §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11: literal-6 "must be nonnumeric and is limited to a single character", may be any character except the digits, "the uppercase letters A, B, C, D, P, R, S, V, X, Z; the lowercase letters a through z; or the space" and * + - , . ; ( ) " = /, and without the clause only the currency sign is the PICTURE currency symbol. SpecialNamesBinder.SwitchBindCurrency binds the bare one-character form (CurrencyOperandOf refuses a numeric literal and a figurative constant, COBOL0892; a longer literal is COBOL0890) and asks ValidateCurrencyChar, which reads the edition's row of CurrencySymbolExclusion: below COBOL-2002 the 1985 list (E and N admitted, every lowercase letter refused, COBOL0891 citing §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11), from 2002 the §2023:12.3.7.3 SR22 list; CurrencySymbolExclusionDriftTests pins both rows to their printed text. PictureAnalyzer.AnalyzeCharacterString and PictureComposition.Validate ask the program's currency symbol before the picture letters, so at 85 E and N (picture symbols only from 2002) are the currency symbol in fixed leading, floating and fixed trailing positions. RegisterCurrency records the symbol, FinalizeCurrencySigns keeps the currency sign as the default, and the 2002 WITH PICTURE SYMBOL phrase is refused at 85 by VisitCurrencySignClause (COBOL0893). Witnesses: CURRENCY SIGN IS "L" with PIC L99 (1985-GR-VI_4_5_4-11), "E" and "N" (pb5173_currency_sign_e_at_85, _n_at_85: [E05][ E12.50][012.50E]) and the refusal of "m" (pb5173_currency_sign_lowercase_refused_at_85, COBOL0891). Outside this rule: two CURRENCY SIGN clauses in one paragraph compile at 85 (the 2002 form; §1985:VI.4.5.2 prints the clause once), the format row's matter.

next.reason: 1985 excludes 'uppercase letters A, B, C, D, P, R, S, V, X, Z; the lowercase letters a through z; or the space'. §2023:12.3.7.3 SR22 excludes 'alphabetic characters A, B, C, D, E, N, P, R, S, V, X, Z, or their lowercase equivalents', with equivalence per §2023:12.3.7.3 SR20. Stricter: CURRENCY SIGN 'E' or 'N' (legal in 1985) is refused. Looser: lowercase letters other than the listed ones (e.g. 'm') are accepted. 1985 'only the currency sign ... may be used' without the clause becomes §2023:12.3.7.3 SR25 (CURRENCY SIGN '$' implied unless some clause names '$', so '$' stays usable beside another currency sign). Literal class per §2023:12.3.7.3 SR18; PICTURE use per §2023:12.3.7.4 GR13. All compile-time.
